selected_claim.claim_verbatim: We just need an anchor tenant or so, and that's it
selected_claim.claim_paraphrase_fair: One or a few large AI data centers would supply enough domestic gas demand to make the ~$44B Alaska LNG pipeline economically viable and financeable.
selected_claim.steelman: A single large AI data center consuming 1-2 GW of power would represent a meaningful, stable baseload gas demand anchor — the kind of offtake commitment that Phase 1 in-state Alaska LNG distribution has always lacked. Unlike export LNG, a domestic anchor tenant would generate in-state revenue, provide a fixed long-term contract, and reduce the financing risk premium on a project whose core problem has always been the absence of committed demand. The governor and the congressional delegation are not wrong that demand certainty is the missing ingredient.
selected_claim.more_accurate_frame: The anchor-tenant thesis assumes gas supply and affordable delivered cost exist to serve large data centers — but Alaska's own utilities are already on record that in-state Cook Inlet gas is unavailable for new large loads, and the only alternative (North Slope pipeline gas) would cost $10–$13.70/MMBtu under Phase 1 estimates, significantly more than current Cook Inlet prices of ~$8.69/MMBtu, making the data center a potential customer for gas Alaska doesn't have at a price that doesn't work.
selected_claim.why_smart_people_believe_it: The pipeline's chronic problem has always been the chicken-and-egg of no committed domestic demand; a hyperscale data center is the first credible large in-state consumer to appear in a generation, and the logic that demand unlocks supply is sound in most energy markets.

counter_evidence.fact: Julie Hasquet, Chugach Electric spokesperson, stated on the record: 'We currently do not have gas to serve a large data center, but we do have generation capacity.' Golden Valley Electric confirmed Cook Inlet gas it relied on dropped from ~30% of its fuel supply to less than 1% last year.

Wood Mackenzie, retained as consultant by AGDC, estimated Phase 1 in-state North Slope pipeline gas would cost $10–$13.70/MMBtu, compared to a current Cook Inlet price of approximately $8.69/MMBtu — meaning pipeline gas would be materially more expensive than the gas it would replace, not cheaper.
counter_evidence.outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Stan Jones op-ed citing Wood Mackenzie/AGDC consultant report)

selected_claim.ak_consequence: Energy sector and capital markets: the anchor-tenant thesis is the load-bearing demand assumption in AGDC's pitch to private investors and the congressional delegation's advocacy for the ~$44B Alaska LNG pipeline; if the assumption fails (no available gas, higher delivered cost than existing supply), the rationale for data-center-linked pipeline financing collapses, directly affecting whether AGDC can attract private capital in 2026–2028 financing windows and whether HB 259 tax incentives are premised on a viable energy supply chain.

dropped_claims.claim_verbatim: We're spilling gigawatt-hours of excess hydropower. This data center can put the excess to use.
dropped_claims.reason: Gate 3 and Gate 5 weak: 170 kW pilot scale with no confirmed replication pipeline; primary counter-evidence URL cited by scouts (nlr.gov) is garbled and unverifiable; rebuttal data comes from the same single CleanTechnica source as the claim. Load-bearing consequence too speculative at current pilot scale.

dropped_claims.claim_verbatim: They are highly capital intensive and employ many in the construction phase, but few for operation.
dropped_claims.reason: Gate 4 fails (true_as_stated): the steelmanned claim is directionally correct; Stak Energy figures (1,500 construction / ~60 permanent) confirm rather than rebut. Brookings counter argues incompleteness, not error. Homer News piece lacked an equivalent verbatim span, weakening circulation. No strong corrective frame survives.

dropped_claims.claim_verbatim: Alaska remains one of the most energy-rich regions in the world.
dropped_claims.reason: Gate 6 fails (recent_repeat): energy-abundance framing substantively identical to the angle corrected in 06-03 (LNG price) and 06-04 (cooling cost/PUE).

dropped_claims.claim_verbatim: Generative AI is transforming how organizations work but without visibility and control, it introduces real security and data risks.
dropped_claims.reason: Gate 3 fails (not_load_bearing): vendor PR assertion from a governance software company's BusinessWire release; does not materially drive a specific Alaska AI capital, procurement, or policy decision. Gate 2 also weak.

dropped_claims.claim_verbatim: Port MacKenzie is one of the few places on Earth where a 10–20 gigawatt AI cluster is physically plausible.
dropped_claims.reason: Gate 2 fails (single_non_primary): single-source op-ed superlative. Gate 5 fails: non-checkable physical-plausibility assertion without a falsifiable primary datum. The Kellerman career-opinion superlative independently fails Gate 5.
